subject: Follow-up: Velox AI deployment path & GPU-mix sizing roadmap
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Matthews <aisha@velox.ai>; James Chen <james.chen@velox.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: Velox AI deployment path & GPU-mix sizing roadmap

Hi Aisha / James,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good discussion. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we don't lose momentum:

- Current leaning: Velox is prioritizing predictable throughput and data isolation for production inference (Dedicated preferred), but compliance teams flagged interest in a Private VPC for auditability.
- Ask from our side: can you share a token/request profile (avg tokens per call, 95th pct, percent long tail) and an expected peak requests-per-second (RPS) target? That will drive GPU mix and concurrency recommendations.

Initial notes based on what you said on the call:
- Workload: mix of short prompt completions (~40–120 tokens) and long-context transforms (~1k+ tokens). You estimated ~200–300 RPS peak with bursts.
- Primary model candidate: Llama-3-70B (we discussed quantized variants).

What we recommend for the next step:
1) Send token-profile CSV and representative sample traces (attach below) — we'll use it to simulate token/sec and latency.
2) We'll run a quick model-fit estimate (Karthik) and propose a 2–3 option SKU mix (A100 vs H100 and GPU counts) showing latency & cost tradeoffs.
3) Sync: 30‑min follow-up next week to agree on a sizing proposal.

Attachments: capacity worksheet (blank) attached — please populate the token mix sheet if possible.

I'll let Karthik own the sizing calc; Laura will track procurement/contract implications if you move to Dedicated.

Thanks,

Michael Grant
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Michael,

Thanks — attaching the token profile and a short QPS trace from last week (spike included). Quick answers:
- Peak RPS (observed): 250 RPS for ~10 minutes; steady-state around 120 RPS.
- Token mix: average 320 tokens/request; 95th percentile ~1,200 tokens; ~12% of calls are >2,000 tokens.
- Compliance: we need VPC peering and customer-managed KMS if we go Private. SOC2 is table stakes.

Questions for you:
1) For caching — will prefix/KV caching meaningfully reduce GPU counts for our workload?
2) Cold-start latency: we're sensitive to tail latency for short prompts — how does Dedicated help vs Hosted?

Files attached: velox_token_profile.csv, velox_qps_trace.json

Thanks,

Velox AI

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Matthews <aisha@velox.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Velox AI deployment path & GPU-mix sizing roadmap

Aisha — appreciate the quick data. I digested the CSV and trace; initial sizing thoughts below.

Short answers first:
- Caching: yes — prefix/KV caching will reduce token work for repeated prefixes (helpful for short prompts). With your mix (12% heavy long calls) caching buys ~15–25% effective token reduction for steady-state traffic, less during large burst windows.
- Cold-start latency: Dedicated with pinned warm workers gives much more predictable tail latency vs multi-tenant Hosted; Dedicated allows more aggressive pre-warming and batching controls.

Sizing sketch (based on Llama-3-70B quantized path):
- Target peak: 250 RPS * 320 tokens/request ~ 80k tokens/sec peak.
- Concurrency: with average request lengths and batching, we expect steady concurrency of ~24–40 inflight requests; set target concurrency headroom to 1.5x for burst tolerance.

GPU option tradeoffs:
1) H100 (best throughput): 3x H100 would give headroom for 80k tokens/sec with ~35–50 ms median token latency under continuous batching; higher upfront cost but lower unit token cost.
2) A100 80GB (memory-conservative): 4x A100 recommended if you prefer lower per-card cost; expect slightly higher token latency and more machines for same throughput.
3) Hybrid: 2x H100 + 1x A100 as a cost-performance compromise (use H100 for heavy long requests and A100 for short prompt-heavy workers).

Operational notes:
- We recommend configuring automatic fallback to a smaller quantized model for very long tail requests if latency is critical.
- We'll model batching window to meet your tail latency SLO; this is what Karthik will simulate.

Next steps (concrete):
- Karthik will run a tokenized throughput simulation and produce a 3-option SKU proposal + back-of-envelope cost by EOD Thursday.
- Laura to produce procurement checklist if you prefer Dedicated vs Private VPC (SLA, KMS, networking ask list).
- Proposed sync: Thu 02/17 10:00 AM PT — I'll send a calendar invite.

If that sounds good I'll kick off the run and attach the preliminary estimate when it's ready.

Best,
Michael
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
